req_desc: The app serves a marketing site for a spreadsheet product.
The app holds no product surface of its own ...
The app links out to a documentation origin ...
The app lets a marketing editor add a sector route with no deploy.
The app offers no comment feature ...
A signed out visitor reads every `published` route ...
A reader reads the trial belonging to that reader ...
An author creates a route ...
The server rejects a reader request to an author only endpoint ...
The app lets anyone create a `reader` account from the signup form.
The app seeds an author account at `author@example.com`.
The app seeds a second author account at `author2@example.com`.
The app seeds a reader account at `reader@example.com`.
Every seeded account signs in with `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
The app issues a bearer token on a successful login ...
A route record carries a `slug` ...
The app serves a `published` route to anyone.
The app serves a `draft` route only to an author ...
Publishing a route stamps `published_at` ...
The app denies a reader request to edit a route ...
The app holds at most one route for a given slug ...
The app carries exactly four templates named `sector`, `capability`, `comparison`, `content` ...
A `sector` route carries the adaptability heading `Custom <sector noun> that adapts to your workflow` ...
A `capability` route carries three numbered steps named `Build`, `Share`, `Analyze` ...
A comparative claim carries its own `source` ...
A content index carries one featured article ...
The home route carries thirteen full-width sections in a fixed order ...
The hero carries the headline `Turn the spreadsheets running your business into secure applications` ...
The capability section carries six third-level headings naming the product capabilities ...
The power tools section carries three third-level headings named `Super-charged formulas`, `Extensible`, `Unprecedented control` ...
The home route names three reference customers, `Northgate Digital Service`, `Merrow Instruments`, `Halliwell Electrical` ...
The home route names three featured templates, `Investment Research Tracker`, `Class Enrolment Register`, `Customer Records Lite` ...
An announcement bar sits above the header on every route ...
The header carries five menu triggers reading `Product`, `Solutions`, `Developers`, `Resources`, `Pricing` ...
A closed menu panel is removed from the focus order ...
The star count control reads a count from `GET /api/stars` ...
Every route other than the home route ends with a band headed `Create a free site` ...
The footer carries multiple link columns ...
Every stored image key follows the scheme `media/{route_id}/{sha256_of_bytes}.{ext}` ...
Uploading identical bytes twice for one route returns the existing key ...
The app denies a reader request to upload an image ...
The app denies a signed out request for an image attached to a `draft` route ...
The app rejects an image saved with no alternative text ...
`POST /api/trials` takes `email`, `team_name`, `sector` ...
The app holds at most one trial for a given team slug ...
A repeated submission of one email with one team name creates no second trial ...
Starting a trial signs a signed out visitor in as a `reader` ...
Every form rejects invalid input inline ...
A first-time visitor is asked once about non essential cookies ...
No third-party script is requested before the cookie answer is accept ...
Every internal link on a published route resolves to a published route ...
The app serves the home route at `/`.
The app serves a template gallery at `/templates/`.
The app serves a sector index at `/solutions/`.
The app serves a comparison route at `/lookup/latticework/`.
The app serves a content index at `/blog/`.
The app serves a case study index at `/case-studies/`.
The app serves a privacy route at `/privacy/` stating what the site stores about a visitor.
The app serves a trial form at `/trial/`.
The app serves a trial confirmation at `/trial/started/` to a reader.
The app serves an authoring console at `/studio/` to an author.
A signed out request for `/studio/` redirects to `/login` ...
The authoring route table lists every route with slug, template, status, last edit.
Every list carries an empty state naming what would appear there ...
The accent colour is a mid, vivid teal ...
One gradient runs teal on the left to green on the right ...
One text family in four weights is declared as a single token ...
Social links are rounded on one diagonal, square on the other ...
Motion character is eased, with movement leaving quickly, arriving slowly ...
Escape closes an open menu panel, returning focus to the trigger ...
Text contrast meets WCAG AA per token pair ...
The build declares four breakpoints as tokens ...
The build commits to a light mode designed in full.
A section style is one of default, light, dark, brand gradient, large pattern, small pattern ...
Every glyph is inline vector.
Four first-party blocks build every section of the home route ...
A closed mega-menu panel stays out of the focus order.
The mark is a three-by-three arrangement of rounded squares with cells omitted.
The build ships no binary asset ...
No feature demonstration ships as an animated raster image ...
The build own stacking scale carries no value above four digits.
The browser receives complete HTML for every public route on first paint ...
`GET /api/health` returns `200` without a token ...
Every response carries a strict transport policy header ...
Read access to unpublished content is decided on the server for every request ...
The app makes no outbound network request at runtime.
The schema carries seven tables ...
The seeded password `deku-demo-pw-2026` works at login ...
The `users` table carries a unique lowercased `email` ...
The `routes` table carries a `slug` unique across the table.
The `sections` table carries a `position` unique within a route ...
The `claims` table requires `source`, `checked_on`.
The `articles` table carries a `kind` of `post`, `webinar`, `case_study` ...
The `media` table holds the pair `(route_id, sha256)` at most once.
The `trials` table carries a `team_slug` unique across the table.
The app seeds nine `published` routes ...
The site is single tenant ...
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL` ...
The HTTP API is served on the same origin under the `/api` prefix.
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready.
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps.
The server keeps running after the session ends ...
The server binds `0.0.0.0`.
`POST /api/auth/login` returns the bearer token as `access_token`.
`GET /api/pages` returns a top-level JSON array of route summaries.
`GET /api/pages/{slug}` returns the route with its `sections` in order.
`POST /api/pages` creates a route at `status` `draft`.
`POST /api/media` returns `{ "object_key" }`.
`POST /api/trials` returns `{ "team_slug", "team_site_url" }`.
`POST /api/consent` stores a `choice` of `accept` or `decline`.
An invalid call is rejected as a client error rather than a server error.
A media object exists in the `MinIO` bucket rather than in an in-memory array ...
core asks covered by this grader
